name: tplc
description: See and control your own TP-Link Kasa and Tapo lights, plugs and outlets, through the open-source tplc CLI.
long_description: Ask Claude what your TP-Link devices are, whether one is on, what a plug draws, and to turn one light, plug or outlet on or off or set a light's brightness or color. Five tools: tplink_devices, tplink_device_state and tplink_energy read; tplink_power and tplink_light change one named device, and Claude asks you before each call. No tool can change a whole strip or several devices at once, control a lock, camera or other model this CLI does not know, edit a schedule or a room, or touch your account. The extension asks for no password: first install the tplc CLI and run `tplc auth login` in a terminal, which stores the session in your OS keychain. The bundled tplc reads it from there and renews it in place. When a session ends, the tools say so; run `tplc auth login` again. What the tools return goes to Claude as part of your conversation. On macOS the first call asks for keychain access, and a renewal asks to write the session back; choose Always Allow for each. A new version of the extension is a new program to the keychain and can ask again. Unofficial; not affiliated with or endorsed by TP-Link.

tools.name: tplink_devices
tools.description: What devices you have: name, kind, online, and what the tools can change on each.

tools.name: tplink_device_state
tools.description: Whether a device is on, with its brightness and color, and a strip's outlets.

tools.name: tplink_energy
tools.description: What a plug or outlet with a meter draws now, or used by day or month.

tools.name: tplink_power
tools.description: Turn one named light, plug, wall switch or outlet on or off, and return the state read back.

tools.name: tplink_light
tools.description: Set one named light's brightness, color or color temperature, and return the state read back.
